hints: Focus on how chlorine and bromine differ in atomic size and number of electrons, since most Group 17 trends follow from this.
Remember that $\text{H-Cl}$ is shorter than $\text{H-Br}$, chlorine holds its outer electron more tightly, and $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute ammonia while $\text{AgBr}$ does not.
Now think about what controls London forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$ molecules, and which element should have the weaker temporary dipoles.
walkthrough:
**Place chlorine and bromine in Group 17**

Chlorine is above bromine in Group 17, so chlorine atoms are smaller with fewer shells and fewer electrons. This one fact controls almost all the trends here.

Trend idea:
$$\text{Cl (Period 3) smaller, fewer electrons than Br (Period 4)}$$

**Compare the first three properties**

The $\text{H-Cl}$ bond is shorter and stronger than $\text{H-Br}$, so bond strength is larger for chlorine. First ionisation energy is also larger for chlorine because the outer electron is closer to the nucleus with less shielding. $\text{AgCl}$ is soluble in dilute $\text{NH}_3(aq)$ but $\text{AgBr}$ needs concentrated $\text{NH}_3(aq)$, so solubility is also larger for chlorine.

**Compare van der Waals forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$**

London (van der Waals) forces get stronger with more electrons and a larger, more polarisable electron cloud. $\text{Br}_2$ has many more electrons than $\text{Cl}_2$, so its temporary dipoles are stronger. That is why $\text{Cl}_2$ is a gas but $\text{Br}_2$ is a liquid at room temperature, and it is the only property here that is smaller for chlorine.

options.A: Incorrect. The $\text{H-Cl}$ bond is stronger than the $\text{H-Br}$ bond because Cl is smaller, so the overlap is better and the bond is shorter. Bond strength therefore decreases down the group, so it is larger, not smaller, for chlorine.
options.B: Incorrect. First ionisation energy decreases down Group 17 because the outer electron in bromine is further from the nucleus and more shielded. Chlorine therefore has the higher first ionisation energy, not the smaller one.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute $\text{NH}_3(aq)$ while $\text{AgBr}$ only dissolves in concentrated $\text{NH}_3(aq)$ and $\text{AgI}$ is insoluble. Solubility in ammonia therefore decreases down the group, so it is larger for chlorine.
options.D: Correct. Van der Waals (London) forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules are weaker than between $\text{Br}_2$ molecules because $\text{Cl}_2$ has fewer electrons and is less polarisable. This is why chlorine is a gas and bromine is a liquid, so this is the only property that is smaller for chlorine than for bromine.
